- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.8) and forecast is high, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.3) and forecast is low, raise forecast modestly to avoid underreaction.  
- If recent price spike is followed by forecast overshoot, apply downward correction by 5–10% of the spike magnitude.  
- If forecast consistently exceeds true outcome by 3–5% over 3–5 days, apply mean reversion bias: subtract 0.5–1.0% per day until convergence.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if true outcome shows early sharp decline after a peak, reduce forecast slope downward by 10–20% in the first 5 days.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, adjust forecast to align with sentiment momentum rather than historical mean.  
- Avoid forecasting based solely on recent 18-day history — incorporate sentiment lag (e.g., 3–5 day sentiment shift) to anticipate direction change.
